# markdownMerge

A deterministic Markdown packer optimized for ChatGPT/OpenAI file uploads.

It recursively scans Markdown sources, preserves their original body content, and packs them into as few upload-safe Markdown files as practical.

## GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 compatibility (checked 2026-11-20)

**ChatGPT GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 can use the Markdown files generated by this tool.** The ChatGPT model selected in the UI is independent of this CLI's tokenizer selection. The CLI's `--model` flag is **not** a ChatGPT model switch; it only asks the installed `tiktoken` package to find an encoding for that name.

**Recommended for both GPT-5.6 and GPT-6:** omit both tokenizer flags (the CLI defaults to `o200k_base`), or explicitly use `--encoding o200k_base`. Do not assume `--model gpt-6` or `--model gpt-5.6` is supported by your installed `tiktoken`; support depends on its model-name mapping. The tokenizer is used to estimate and validate packaging size, not to set the model's context window.

The ChatGPT text/document **upload ceiling remains 2,000,000 tokens and 512 MB per file**, independently of the chosen chat model. Upload eligibility is distinct from how much text can be actively considered in one answer. For current model access and quotas, consult [GPT-6 and other models](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001354-gpt-6-and-other-models-in-chatgpt) and [file uploads](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545-uploading-files-and-audio-to-chatgpt).

## Default ChatGPT/OpenAI profile

Current defaults intentionally stay below the official per-file upload ceilings:

- final token target: 1,800,000 tokens
- planning reserve: 50,000 tokens
- effective packing budget: 1,750,000 tokens
- tokenizer: o200k_base
- hard byte validation: 512,000,000 bytes (512 MB) per generated file

OpenAI currently documents a 2,000,000-token cap for text/document uploads and a 512 MB hard file-size limit. The defaults leave token headroom rather than targeting the absolute ceiling.

## Daily usage

### Everyday recommended command (GPT-5.6 or GPT-6)

After installing `mdmerge`, run from a directory **outside** the input folder:

```bash
mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-upload --name docs --token-limit 100000 --reserve-tokens 5000
```

This is a **practical optional preset**, not a new built-in default or an official model limit. It aims for an effective packing budget of 95,000 tokens per file. Choose it when you want to inspect or upload relevant parts selectively. If you prefer fewer output files for an archive, use `mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-upload` and retain the built-in 1.8-million-token ceiling.

Daily workflow: (1) collect or update your source `.md` files, (2) run the command, (3) check `validation.txt` and `manifest.json`, (4) upload only the numbered `.md` parts you need, (5) ask ChatGPT to reference `# Source:` markers. Re-running regenerates the output files; check for obsolete numbered parts from earlier runs before uploading the directory's contents.


### Install once for use from any directory

```bash
uv tool install --editable /home/murat/Project/docsync/markdownMerge
```

Make sure the uv tool executable directory is on your PATH (`uv tool update-shell` can configure it), then use `mdmerge` directly from anywhere. `uv run mdmerge` is for running within a project environment that contains the command.

### Default: automatically create an output folder

```bash
mdmerge /home/murat/Library/Documents/Notes/Murat/Google/Documentation/ai.google
```

The output is written into a directory named after the input folder inside the current working directory (`pwd`). The directory is created automatically when missing:

```text
<pwd>/ai.google/
├── ai.google-1.md
├── manifest.json
├── summary.txt
└── validation.txt
```

### Custom output: use the exact specified directory

```bash
mdmerge /home/murat/Library/Documents/Notes/Murat/Google/Documentation/ai.google \
  --output /path/to/custom-output
```

The specified directory and any missing parent directories are created automatically. No input-directory-name subfolder is added when `--output` is supplied.

### Run without global installation

```bash
cd /home/murat/Project/docsync/markdownMerge
uv sync
uv run mdmerge /path/to/site-markdown
```

This default output directory is `/home/murat/Project/docsync/markdownMerge/<input-directory-name>/` because that is the working directory in this example. To place output elsewhere, use `--output`.

Generated files are numbered `<input-name>-1.md`, `<input-name>-2.md`, and so on as needed, alongside `manifest.json`, `summary.txt`, and `validation.txt`. If all sources fit in one part, only `<input-name>-1.md` is generated.

## ChatGPT usage recipes (2026)

The following commands use the existing CLI; no new flags are required.

### Quick start on any machine

From the repository checkout:

```bash
cd markdownMerge
uv sync
uv run mdmerge --help
uv run mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-upload
```

For a global command, install from your local checkout rather than copying a machine-specific absolute path:

```bash
uv tool install --editable ./markdownMerge
mdmerge --help
mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-upload
```

Run the installation command from the repository root. For `uv run`, run inside `markdownMerge/`.

### CLI argument reference

| Argument | Required? | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INPUT_DIRECTORY` | Yes | — | Recursively scan Markdown files in this folder. |
| `--output PATH` | No | `./<input-directory-name>` | Write output parts and reports to this directory. |
| `--name NAME` | No | Input folder name | Filename prefix for numbered Markdown parts; do not include `.md` or path separators. |
| `--token-limit N` | No | `1800000` | Maximum final tokens per output file. Must be positive. |
| `--reserve-tokens N` | No | `50000` | Unused planning headroom; must be nonnegative and smaller than the token limit. |
| `--model MODEL` | No | — | Select a tokenizer using `tiktoken.encoding_for_model`. |
| `--encoding NAME` | No | `o200k_base` | Select an explicit tiktoken encoding. Cannot be combined with `--model`. |
| `--help` / `-h` | No | — | Print CLI usage and available options. |

The effective packing budget is `--token-limit - --reserve-tokens`. The final written parts are re-tokenized and checked against the final token ceiling and byte limit. Model names only select a tokenizer: they do **not** change ChatGPT's upload limits or guarantee that all uploaded text fits in a model's active context.

### Practical commands

```bash
# Default: preserve content and pack into as few parts as practical
mdmerge ./docs

# Choose an output location and readable part names
mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-upload --name project-docs

# Smaller files for easier per-part review or retrieval
mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-small --token-limit 100000 --reserve-tokens 5000

# Explicitly use the default tokenizer
mdmerge ./docs --encoding o200k_base

# GPT-5.6 / GPT-6: use a known encoding (does not select ChatGPT's model)
mdmerge ./docs --encoding o200k_base

# Optional: select a model mapping known to your installed tiktoken version
mdmerge ./docs --model gpt-4o
```

The 100,000-token example is an **optional workflow choice**, not an official ChatGPT file cap. For large corpora, smaller parts can be easier to navigate, but they produce more uploads.

### Daily presets and when to use them

| Workflow | Example options | Effective token budget per part | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Focused review | `--token-limit 50000 --reserve-tokens 5000` | 45,000 | More parts, easier to select relevant documents |
| Everyday ChatGPT work | `--token-limit 100000 --reserve-tokens 5000` | 95,000 | Practical starting point, not a guaranteed context fit |
| Larger reference packages | `--token-limit 250000 --reserve-tokens 10000` | 240,000 | Fewer parts, potentially harder to inspect |
| Maximum packing (built-in default) | No token flags | 1,750,000 | Minimizes parts heuristically, but may exceed active context |

All rows still use the CLI's independent byte validation. These are **workflow suggestions**, not GPT-5.6/GPT-6 context-window specifications.

### Verify before uploading to ChatGPT

Check `validation.txt` for a passing result and `manifest.json` for `"upload_ready": true`. Upload the generated `<name>-1.md`, `<name>-2.md`, etc. to your ChatGPT conversation, Project, or custom GPT knowledge as appropriate. The reports are local metadata, not required uploads.

ChatGPT's documented per-file maximum for text/document uploads is **2 million tokens and 512 MB**. These are upload ceilings, **not** a promise that a model can read every token at once. The default 1.8-million-token target leaves headroom beneath the per-file ceiling; for focused question answering, consider smaller chunks. ChatGPT Projects, GPT knowledge, and upload-rate quotas have separate file-count limits that depend on product and plan. As documented at the time of this update, Projects allow 5 files on Free, 25 on Go/Plus, and 40 on Edu/Pro/Business/Enterprise; custom GPT knowledge allows 20 files. No more than 10 files can be uploaded to a Project at once. Limits may change. Check the [official file upload documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545-uploading-files-and-audio-to-chatgpt) before preparing a large batch.

Example prompt after upload:

> Use the uploaded Markdown packages as reference material. Cite the `# Source: relative/path.md` markers when answering. If a source is split across packages, check all relevant chunks. Do not assume the entire corpus is in the current model context.

### Repeatable shell workflow (optional)

Run from your repository root after installing the CLI:

```bash
# Prepare and validate a fresh daily package
mdmerge ./docs --output ./chatgpt-upload --name docs \
  --token-limit 100000 --reserve-tokens 5000

# Read the generated reports
cat ./chatgpt-upload/validation.txt
cat ./chatgpt-upload/summary.txt

# Inspect upload readiness (requires Python 3)
python -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("chatgpt-upload/manifest.json"))["upload_ready"])'
```

A printed `True` indicates that the tool's own validation passed; it does not guarantee ChatGPT will accept the batch under your plan's remaining quota. If an older run produced more numbered parts than the current run, remove obsolete output files manually or use a new empty output directory before each run. Do not delete your source folder.

### Common pitfalls

- **Output directory inside input directory:** choose an output path outside the scanned input tree; the CLI rejects overlapping paths.
- **No Markdown files found:** confirm the input path contains `.md` files.
- **Invalid reserve:** `--reserve-tokens` must be smaller than `--token-limit`.
- **GPT-6/GPT-5.6 names:** do not use `--model gpt-6` or `--model gpt-5.6` unless your installed `tiktoken` explicitly recognizes them; `--encoding o200k_base` is the documented safe choice for this tool.
- **Tokenizer options:** choose either `--model` or `--encoding`, not both.
- **Too many upload parts:** increase the token budget (within the documented upload ceiling) or upload relevant subsets; do not assume ChatGPT can process an arbitrarily large corpus in one context.
- **Validation failed:** inspect `validation.txt` before uploading. Do not treat the output as upload-ready.

## Packing behavior

1. Recursively discover all `.md` sources.
2. Preserve each source body exactly.
3. Prefix each source or chunk with a traceability marker:
   `# Source: relative/path.md`.
4. Split only an individual source that cannot fit inside the effective token budget, tokenizing oversized content once and preserving exact UTF-8 source bytes.
5. Pack normal sources and oversized-source chunks together with deterministic First-Fit Decreasing.
6. Re-tokenize the written output.
7. Validate both token count and 512 MB byte size.
8. Mark the run `upload_ready: true` in `manifest.json` only when validation passes.

First-Fit Decreasing is a deterministic packing heuristic and normally produces a small number of parts, though it does not mathematically guarantee the absolute minimum bin count for every possible input.

## Source integrity

markdownMerge does not summarize, rewrite, normalize, or remove source content. It does not alter code blocks. Only sources too large for one package are split into ordered chunks. Split output is checked for byte-for-byte UTF-8 continuity before writing.

## Optional overrides

The default command needs only an input directory. Advanced overrides remain available:

```bash
uv run mdmerge INPUT_DIRECTORY \
  [--name NAME] \
  [--output OUTPUT_DIRECTORY] \
  [--token-limit TOKEN_LIMIT] \
  [--reserve-tokens RESERVE_TOKENS] \
  [--model MODEL | --encoding ENCODING_NAME]
```

Example with explicit defaults:

```bash
uv run mdmerge ./docs \
  --token-limit 1800000 \
  --reserve-tokens 50000 \
  --encoding o200k_base
```

## Validation and metadata

`validation.txt` reports tokens, bytes, source-marker count, and status for every generated Markdown file.

`manifest.json` records:

- input directory
- token limit and effective token limit
- reserve tokens
- maximum file bytes
- tokenizer
- input file count
- generated part count
- per-part tokens and bytes
- source membership
- validation state
- `upload_ready`

## Development

```bash
cd /home/murat/Project/docsync/markdownMerge
uv sync --group dev
./quality.sh
```

The quality pipeline checks formatting, linting, strict type checking, tests, and CLI entry points.

### Reference benchmark

On the `developers.openai.com` corpus used during v1.0 validation (1,485 Markdown files), the oversized-source splitter optimization reduced the end-to-end run from 5m48s to 1m09.834s (about 5x faster). The optimized run completed with `Validation Result: PASSED`. Benchmark results are workload- and machine-dependent.

## Scope

markdownMerge only prepares local Markdown packages. It does not upload files, call OpenAI APIs, crawl websites, summarize content, or modify source prose.
